title: Faithfully flat tensor model criterion for a surjective source map
statement: Let $R,C,P,A,D,B$ be commutative rings, with ring maps $R\to P\xrightarrow{\varphi}A\xrightarrow{f}B$, $C\to P$, $C\to D$ and $g:D\to B$, such that the two induced maps $C\to B$ agree. Give $A$ its $C$-algebra structure through $P$, and give $B$ its $R$-algebra structure through $P$ and $A$. Suppose $C\to D$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and the induced $A$-algebra map $e:A\otimes_C D\to B$, $a\otimes d\mapsto f(a)g(d)$, is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ over $R$, and put $Q=P\otimes_C D$ and $q:Q\to B$, $p\otimes d\mapsto f(\varphi(p))g(d)$. Assume elements $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in Q$ satisfy $q(z_j)=b_j$. Then $P\to Q$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, is faithfully flat, $q$ is surjective, and there is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:A\otimes_P Q\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $\theta(a\otimes(p\otimes d))=e(a\varphi(p)\otimes d)$ and inverse given by $\theta^{-1}(e(a\otimes d))=a\otimes(1\otimes d)$. It satisfies $\theta(1\otimes z)=q(z)$ for every $z\in Q$, so the base change of $\varphi$ identifies with $q$; moreover $\varphi$ is surjective. If $p_1,\ldots,p_N$ generate $P$ over $R$, then $\varphi(p_1),\ldots,\varphi(p_N)$ generate $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Tensor products and the induced maps use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the indicated algebra structures. No finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], the compatible maps $P\to B$ and $D\to B$ induce $q$. It is an $R$-algebra map: on $r\in R$ its value at $r_P\otimes1$ is $f(\varphi(r_P))=r_B$. For any $b\in B$, the generating hypothesis means $b=F(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ for a polynomial $F$ over $R$, by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Hence $q(F(z_1,\ldots,z_n))=F(b_1,\ldots,b_n)=b$. Thus $q$ is surjective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] with its $R=C$, $S=D$, $R\prime=P$. The hypothesis is precisely the assumed faithful flatness of $C\to D$, and the other map is $C\to P$. It gives faithful flatness of $P\to Q=P\otimes_C D$, with $p\mapsto p\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 0367, lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra, proof, final paragraph (lines 4370–4381): finite-generator enlargement, tensor comparison, reflection of surjectivity, and finite generation of the quotient.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] to $C\to P$, the $C$-algebra $D$ and the $P$-algebra $A$. It gives an $A$-algebra isomorphism $c:A\otimes_P Q\to A\otimes_C D$, $a\otimes(p\otimes d)\mapsto a\varphi(p)\otimes d$, with inverse $a\otimes d\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes d)$. Set $\theta=e\circ c$; composing the stated inverse with $e^{-1}$ gives exactly the required inverse formula. For $z=p\otimes d$, $\theta(1\otimes z)=e(\varphi(p)\otimes d)=q(z)$. Both sides are additive and $C$-linear in $z$, so the equality holds for every $z$ because pure tensors generate, by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This identifies the base-change map $Q\to A\otimes_P Q$ with $q$.

source.place: Tag 0367, lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra, proof, final paragraph (lines 4370–4381): finite-generator enlargement, tensor comparison, reflection of surjectivity, and finite generation of the quotient.

proof.text: Let $\lambda=\varphi\otimes_C\mathrm{id}_D:P\otimes_C D\to A\otimes_C D$, as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On $p\otimes d$, $e\lambda(p\otimes d)=f(\varphi(p))g(d)=q(p\otimes d)$; hence $e\lambda=q$ on all tensors. Since $e$ is bijective and $q$ is surjective, $\lambda$ is surjective. The natural swap isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm] identify it with $\mathrm{id}_D\otimes_C\varphi$. Apply the exactness-reflection clause of [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] to the complex of $C$-modules $P\xrightarrow{\varphi}A\to0$: after tensoring with $D$ it is exact at $D\otimes_C A$ by that surjectivity ($D\otimes_C0=0$, since all its generating pure tensors are zero). Consequently the original complex is exact at $A$, which says $\operatorname{im}\varphi=A$.

proof.text: If $p_1,\ldots,p_N$ generate $P$ over $R$, take $a\in A$ and choose $p\in P$ with $\varphi(p)=a$, using step 4. Write $p=F(p_1,\ldots,p_N)$ with coefficients in $R$. Since $\varphi$ respects the $R$-structure, $a=F(\varphi(p_1),\ldots,\varphi(p_N))$. Thus these images generate $A$, in the polynomial sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].
